A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToEdit research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data mixture training, distribution analyses, and ToEdit pre-training, continual-pre-training, and fine-tuning experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds instruction-tuning performance across editing generations in Table 16.

M1.justification: The conditional-probability threshold rule, token resampling, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Both versions use a single non-autoregressive forward pass with the same default threshold and sampling strategy.

E1.justification: The training corpora, biomedical/finance/math domains, instruction-tuning and code-related tasks, and evaluation benchmarks are retained. The added iterative-performance table extends analysis within existing instruction-tuning coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated original-data controls, sampling alternatives, and DSIR, education-classifier, PPL-filter, and density-sampling comparisons remain. The latter comparison is preserved in v1 Table 13 and v2 Table 14. Newly cited methods are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 Table 16 extends reported instruction-tuning evaluation to a second editing generation. The reported threshold sweep also drops the p <= 0.001 configuration. Existing model sizes, training budgets, benchmarks, and evaluation metrics otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds performance across editing generations (Table 16) alongside the retained edited-token-count analysis, plus a concrete editing case study (Table 12). Conversely, v1 Table 7's p <= 0.001 ablation is absent from v2 Table 5. Other sensitivity and sampling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 4A adds visible capped error bars to the PPL comparison previously shown without them in v1 Figure 4B. Their meaning and associated run counts are not specified. The standard-error reporting in Table 11 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Most benchmark scores are unchanged. v2 Table 16 adds Gen 2 results averaging 69.39; Gen 0 and Gen 1 reproduce existing CoT results. The removed threshold row averaged 39.16, exceeding the retained default's 38.69. Table 1 adds and changes Avg entries despite unchanged domain scores; its new averages do not match the displayed block means.

T1.justification: The linear-model assumptions, two theorems, error bounds, and Appendix A derivations are substantively unchanged. The KL-based synthetic-data definitions and entropy lemma move to Appendices D and G.2 rather than being removed or replaced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim non-iterative degradation from synthetic-data mixtures, restricted distribution coverage and concentrated features, and theoretically bounded error with useful token editing. Consolidating the contribution bullets and renaming 'coverage collapse' to 'coverage narrowing' do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: New Appendices G.8–G.9 discuss already-collapsed data, describe threshold adjustment as an unvalidated possibility, and explain difficulties separating informative long-tail samples from noise. Existing coherence concerns and applicability to partially synthetic source data remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit ToEdit code-repository link in the introduction. Most implementation and training disclosures are retained or relocated, including vLLM, GPU information, sampling parameters, training frameworks, and LoRA usage. The PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents.

R1.justification: The background and Appendix B substantially broaden coverage to verification-based filtering, iterative stability, curated-data preference optimization, training workflows, and feedback-based self-training. Newly discussed works include Feng, Bertrand, Ferbach, Kazdan, Seddik, and ReST. Appendix H also expands application references; these are contextual additions, not experimental comparisons.

P1.justification: v2 creates an early Background section, moves the main Discussion and detailed numerical interpretation into appendices, reorganizes related work, and condenses several main-text passages. Terminology changes to 'coverage narrowing.' These changes substantially restructure the narrative.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to two-column layout, Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 2's training-loss panel moves to the appendix, and Figure 4 becomes a bar chart with a corrected PPL scale. Tables are extensively reformatted and relocated. New displays include the editing example, iterative results, and a donut chart of existing token statistics.

improvement.justification: The added iterative evidence, broader context, applicability discussion, code pointer, and revised figures offer benefits. However, v2 removes the highest-average threshold ablation without explanation and introduces inconsistent Table 1 averages: its first human-data block reports 20.99 although the displayed scores average 20.43. These reporting regressions coexist with documentation and presentation gains, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
